name: Energy-Mission Machineries (India) Limited
summary: Energy-Mission Machineries (India) Limited is a real sheet-metal forming machinery manufacturer, not an energy developer. Its engineering range, domestic servicing and dispersed historical customers provide a credible franchise, but not yet demonstrated high-return compounding. The decisive risk is that inventory and incremental capital have grown much faster than owner cash earnings. At the 19 October 2026 close of ₹115.85, the base assumption set produces 13.93% annualized equity return against a 15% hurdle. BQS is 5.02 and GQS 5.00 after the persistent-cash-conversion cap. R and IAS are NS because the current funding bridge is unverified; the classification is Hold — unresolved, not a numeric matrix verdict. The illustrative return is not an evidence-supported current funded case. This is a cyclical manufacturing/capacity-utilization thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. A verified working-capital release, mature returns from commissioned facilities and current funding evidence could improve the conclusion; an attractive headline P/E alone does not. [S1,S4,S5,S16]
priority: Research watchlist; current funding evidence hold
identity_note: Official NSE ISIN, active SM series and issued capital independently extracted.

quote.kind: Official closing price; not an executable quote

score_note: BQS/GQS quality-comparison eligible. R and IAS NS for material current-funding uncertainty; IAS coverage 65%, bounds 3.205–6.355. Model returns are assumption-dependent illustrations, not supported current funded returns.

gates.reason: Documented controls/compliance concerns require follow-up, but unmodified audit, operating audit trail and no reported default are favorable. No severe-abuse finding or governance override.

Audited operating history is usable at Medium confidence after explicit scope, restatement and cash-flow classification adjustments. MSME reconciliation and a small unaudited subsidiary limit precision but do not invalidate every quality factor.

Base and restrained operations are funded under explicit assumptions, while linked stress is not. March balance sheet is stale by 202 days; current unrestricted cash, remaining IPO earmarks, commissioning cash and lender maturity/headroom confirmations are needed for implementation. This is not a proven funding failure.
Dated official trading and lot data are complete; a 5 lakh reference position is slow to exit. Current executable spread/depth, circuit availability and user position remain unverified.

positive_evidence: Unmodified FY26 opinion, functioning audit trail and no reported loan default; promoter stake 73.76% in March, with no disclosed pledge.
IPO was entirely fresh capital; three executive salaries remained 1.20 crore each.
counterevidence: Long-standing professional-tax arrears, high related-party remuneration, a new 0.1905 crore subsidiary director loan and unresolved MSME/loan reconciliations.
Small USA financials are management-certified, not separately audited. Intercompany approvals are broad.
GOV.reason: Adequate but material stewardship/documentation concerns; no sufficient evidence for severe integrity failure or a GOV ≤3 override.

positive_evidence: Established in-house manufacturing, customization, domestic service network and dispersed historical customers.
counterevidence: No long-term customer contracts; European/Japanese/import and domestic alternatives. Low service revenue, substantial inventory and below-cost incremental returns do not prove pricing power.
MOAT.reason: Useful manufacturing/service franchise, but contestable advantages rather than a structural moat.

positive_evidence: Five-year same-parent revenue CAGR 27.28%, starting rubric 8; revenue grew from 47.61 to 159.08 crore.
counterevidence: COVID FY21 base flatters the five-year figure; three-year CAGR is 16.91%. Both FY26 half-years slowed to single-digit revenue growth.
REV.reason: Window chosen before scoring: five-year comparable standalone; apply one net point downward for two-half-year trajectory, not another small-base haircut. 8 - 1 = 7.

positive_evidence: Broad fabrication end markets, more machines possible within announced 1,500-unit capacity, and a management-reported commissioned backward-integration facility.
counterevidence: Orders remain discretionary customer capex; latest 47.23 crore book is only about 3.5 months of FY26 sales, with no cancellation/collection schedule. Exports remain small.
DUR.reason: Accessible moderate runway, constrained by cyclical demand and capital-intensive execution; TAM claims do not earn a score increase.

positive_evidence: FY26 post-tax operating ROIC is about 11.88%; CWIP has not yet matured, so a lagged recovery is plausible.
counterevidence: FY25–FY26 incremental NOPAT 0.52065 crore on 19.6149 crore additional operating capital is 2.65%; three-year fully reconciled incremental operating return is 6.47%, and five-year is 12.78%.
CAP.reason: Recent incremental economics remain below a reasoned nominal INR 13–17% capital-cost range. Expansion immaturity is a countercase, not proof of excess returns.

positive_evidence: FY26 reported CFO recovered to 14.76 crore and receivables released 3.43 crore.
counterevidence: FY24–FY26 cumulative CFO only 2.05 crore versus PAT 34.76 crore; inventory remains 76.20 crore and older receivables are unprovided.
CASH.reason: Persistent multi-year poor realization, not merely investing capex, supports 3 and the GQS cap at 5.

positive_evidence: Reported EBIT/finance cover 7.12 times; no audit-reported default; restrained essential-operation illustration is funded only under the unverified current bridge.
counterevidence: Drawn debt 29.71 crore, including 18.18 crore demand cash credit; only 2.75 crore cash before possible IPO earmarks. Collection stress creates a modeled shortfall.
BAL.reason: Manageable disclosed base, not resilient to credible stress. October cash and lender headroom are not verified.

positive_evidence: Capacity enlargement and June 2026 backward integration were reported as completed; actual sales continued growing.
counterevidence: Expansion has not delivered strong per-share profits or cash over the comparable period; facility timing slipped from January completion language, and order book declined from September 2025.
EXEC.reason: Mixed delivery. Commissioning is distinguished from realized output, utilization, cost savings and collections.

positive_evidence: Most reported profit is operating rather than other income; normalized FY26 PAT about 12.09 crore.
counterevidence: FY26 group PAT up only 0.63%; standalone PAT fell. Reported EPS nearly flat and H2 group PAT fell around 11.25%.
EARN.reason: Recurring operating profit exists, but recent per-share compounding is weak after IPO dilution and increased capital.

positive_evidence: The transparent illustration yields 13.93% with no assumed new financing or multiple expansion; it is useful for sensitivities, not proof of a funded current opportunity.
counterevidence: Actual October cash, operating working capital, incremental commissioning spend and remaining IPO restrictions are unverified. An additional 2 crore prequote capex is arithmetically funded, but 4 crore creates a shortfall.
R.reason: NS: missing current funding evidence is material to whether any ordinary return exists. A mathematically consistent assumption set cannot substitute for verified financing capacity.

positive_evidence: Flat-sales essential operations can service disclosed debt at modeled pace; a guarantee call alone is manageable.
counterevidence: Linked bear requires 1.53 crore extra equity; 15 extra receivable days cause a 1.18 crore shortfall. Conditional bear rescue terminal price 87.69, 24.3% below entry.
D.reason: Material capital-impairment and recapitalization exposure at this price, without asserting actual default.

positive_evidence: Roughly 11x reported earnings and 7x operating EBITDA are not extreme headline multiples.
counterevidence: 15% hurdle needs about 9.38% growth at unchanged capital intensity and 7x exit, above FY26 growth; 5x exit cuts base return to 6.92%.
P.reason: Price assumes fair execution, with limited margin for error, not implausible hypergrowth.

positive_evidence: All 60 completed market sessions have trades; current lot independently verified at 250 shares.
counterevidence: Lower 60-day turnover is median 9.05 lakh/day; 5% reference exit takes 11.05 sessions before spread/circuits, and whole-lot median allows one lot/day.
L.reason: Lower anchor of the >10 to 20-session band. No upper-band reward for the better recent 20-day period; execution remains conditional.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Energy-Mission Machineries (India) Limited; CIN L29100GJ2011PLC063696; ISIN INE0S1L01013; NSE Emerge symbol EMMIL, active SM series. Some issuer boilerplate says BSE or Ind AS; the exchange master and actual audit accounting policy take precedence. Price ₹115.85 is an observed 19 October 2026 close, not an executable quote. Current issued shares 11,326,500, market capitalization ₹131.22 crore, face value ₹10 and lot 250 shares. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026; later retrieval dates do not authorize later information.
Financial perimeter: FY21–FY23 prospectus-restated standalone; FY24–FY26 consolidated with two wholly owned subsidiaries; the selected growth CAGR uses the same parent standalone throughout. Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not Ind AS. FY26 audit dated 26 May 2026, annual report filed 5 September. The USA subsidiary's ₹1.90 crore assets and ₹3.51 crore revenue were management-certified and deemed immaterial by the auditor.
G1 Conditional; G2 Conditional; G3 Hold pending current cash/funding bridge; G4 Conditional. Confidence is High on identity, dated price, share count and actual turnover; Medium on audited economics after accounting reconciliation, moat, governance and prospective operations; Low on present cash availability and post-commissioning cash conversion. Horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, nominal INR equity hurdle 15%, before personal taxes, ₹5 lakh illustrative liquidity reference. No actual position or suitability assumption is made.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5; IAS components R NS, D 4, P 5 and L 3. Each has positive evidence, counterevidence and a source-specific confidence assessment in factor_audit.
BQS contributions: 1.00 + 1.00 + 0.84 + 0.60 + 0.48 + 0.30 + 0.40 + 0.40 = 5.02. GQS raw: 2.80 + 1.20 + 0.75 + 0.60 + 0.30 = 5.65. Persistent poor operating cash realization makes CASH 3, so the prescribed cap produces final GQS 5.00. IAS is NS: known contributions 1.255 + 0.80 + 0.50 + 0.30 = 2.855 cover 65% of the weight. The unknown 35% R weight produces bounds 3.205–6.355, not a midpoint or a reweighted score. BQS/GQS coverage is 100%; their half-up one-decimal displays are 5.0 / 5.0. No unknown is replaced by a neutral score and no post hoc haircut is used.
All quality inputs are scoreable at Medium confidence or better, so BQS/GQS may enter provisional quality comparisons. IAS is NS and excluded from investment ranking until current funding evidence supports a scoreable R. The retained illustration is useful for sensitivity analysis but cannot establish a supported current return. Moving the two most uncertain supported factors, CAP and MOAT, together by one point changes BQS to 4.70–5.34; GQS remains capped at 5, and IAS stays NS. Such nearby quality differences should not be overinterpreted. No G1 or proven G3-failure cap is applied. All batch rankings remain provisional.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company designs and manufactures hydraulic/CNC press brakes, shearing machines, plate-rolling machines, ironworkers, presses and customized forming systems at Sanand, Gujarat. It traces its business to 1998 and incorporation to 2011. Manufacturing includes fabrication, machining, hydraulic cylinders/power packs, electrical panels, assembly and testing; selected surface-treatment and specialist processes are outsourced. Thus the business is more than trading, but is not fully vertically integrated.
FY26 audited revenue ₹160.85 crore comprises products ₹159.12 crore and services ₹1.72 crore. Press brakes contributed ₹117.49 crore, shearing ₹25.24 crore, other products ₹16.40 crore. Repair/maintenance itself was only ₹0.36 crore; freight, packing and insurance also sit within services. The presentation's parts/service mix is not an audited recurring-annuity measure. FY26 FOB exports were about ₹5.70 crore, roughly 3.5% of group revenue, so overseas opportunity is not current dominant earnings.
The prospectus describes 1,657 machines supplied to over 1,150 customers during FY21–December 2023, with 29 sales staff and 22 service staff in March 2024. Customers span fabrication, infrastructure, engineering, automobiles, electrical equipment and pre-engineered buildings. Historical top-ten customers were only 9.41% of FY23 sales, but no long-term customer contracts were in place. Orders, advances, dispatch, installation and subsequent collections are separate events: ₹8.48 crore customer advances are an obligation to deliver, not free equity cash. Two subsidiaries are wholly owned: EM Press Form Solutions for fabrication/backward integration and Energy Mission Machineries USA for market access. Intercompany sales must not be added to consolidated revenue.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
A plausible advantage is affordable customized machinery with local service and an installed base, rather than patents, network effects or locked-in software economics. In-house fabrication/machining and an experienced team can improve lead times and quality. The burden of proof remains actual repeat economics, warranty performance, realized pricing and returns, not descriptions such as indigenous innovation or world-class quality. Management's roughly 30% repeat-order claim is not an audited cohort retention measure.
The prospectus names Hindustan Hydraulics, Rajesh Machine Tools, HACO and Weldor as competitors. Global machines from Amada, Trumpf and LVD plus Turkish/Chinese imports provide technological or price alternatives. No independently verified market-share series, customer switching-cost study or service annuity is supplied. Top-ten suppliers accounted for 54.33% of FY23 purchases and had no long-term supply contracts, so sourcing concentration is more substantial than customer concentration.
Macpower is an adjacent metal-cutting CNC manufacturer, not an identical forming-machinery peer. Its FY26 standalone revenue ₹333.18 crore, PAT ₹33.87 crore and CFO ₹14.03 crore show both larger scale and only 0.41x one-year conversion; low borrowing alone does not prove excellent working-capital economics. At the same dated ₹1,826.50 close and 10,004,160 issued shares, its reported P/E is about 54x. Rajoo is plastic extrusion equipment, not metal forming: FY26 group revenue ₹344.25 crore, group PAT ₹48.90 crore and CFO ₹67.81 crore, but acquisitions, ₹119.30 crore goodwill, minority interests and rising customer-linked liabilities confound organic comparison. Its ₹59.95 dated close implies roughly 22.4x owner PAT, using 178,675,293 current shares. These are contextual multiples, not transferable targets.
Jyoti is a much larger CNC group with different complexity and international exposure; its FY26 auditor highlights an ongoing subsidiary investigation and associated restrictions without modifying the opinion. An investigation is not a conviction. The lesson is to compare business mix, cash, claims and governance, not import the highest peer multiple. EMMIL's base exit remains 7x operating EBITDA, around its own current level.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Same-parent standalone revenue was ₹47.61, ₹78.35, ₹99.56, ₹126.29, ₹150.49 and ₹159.08 crore in FY21 through FY26. Annual additions were ₹30.74, ₹21.21, ₹26.73, ₹24.20 and ₹8.58 crore. The five-year CAGR is 27.28%, four-year 19.37%, and three-year 16.91%. FY21 was a COVID-affected base; this is disclosed rather than silently changing the scoring window. Five-year rubric 8 is reduced once to 7 for the sustained latest slowdown.
Group FY26 revenue grew 6.43% to ₹160.85 crore; standalone grew 5.70%. Two comparable group half-years grew 4.15% and approximately 8.55%. H1 FY26 revenue/PAT were ₹75.85/₹6.42 crore; derived H2 were ₹85.00/₹5.51 crore versus prior H2 ₹78.30/₹6.21 crore. H2 PAT therefore fell about 11.25%. The December 2025 deck's headline H1 PAT growth 16.49% conflicts with its own detailed table: ₹6.4217/₹5.6478 implies 13.70%; the detailed values govern.
H1 FY26 management reported 368 machines sold and approximately ₹19.6 lakh ASP, with volume up around 8% and ASP down around 3%. This supports physical demand rather than mere price inflation, but complete FY26 audited unit output and FY27 H1 results were not located by cutoff. No seasonal half-year is annualized as observed TTM growth. New subsidiaries are organically established, not an identified external acquisition; group and parent histories remain separate.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The bottom-up opportunity is to sell more forming equipment through a larger assembly/fabrication footprint, improve throughput and reduce outsourced job work. The prospectus's engineer-certified table gives FY23 output 490 against 900 capacity, or 54.44%; its table labels quantities as Mt while narrative refers to machines, so the unit ambiguity is preserved. Management subsequently reports capacity 1,500 machines per year, effective July 2025, and a 5,000-square-meter backward-integration facility operational in June 2026. This establishes a reported commissioning milestone, not independently verified sustainable output or collections. Its claimed 30–40% backward integration is not the same as a 30–40% margin gain.
Audited group job work fell from ₹7.68 crore in FY25 to ₹6.62 crore in FY26. Management's ₹7.62 to ₹5.97 crore figures appear to reflect a narrower/standalone perimeter; they are not substituted for the consolidated audited expense. Proposed further savings are forecasts. The 27 August 2026 book of ₹47.23 crore is down from the September 2025 ₹55.75 crore disclosure and covers only about 3.5 months of trailing revenue; order intake, order backlog and cash receipts are not interchangeable.
Base growth of 8% yields year-five sales ₹236.34 crore, requiring around 1,125 equivalent machines at ₹21 lakh average revenue per unit before mix/services. Bull sales ₹283.47 crore imply around 1,350 units at that illustrative realization, near the claimed 1,500 capacity. Neither unit calculation is an audited production forecast. The bull additionally needs 17% EBITDA margin and working-capital intensity falling to 40%; it is not justified solely by spare capacity.
FY26 operating ROIC about 11.88% is below the analytical 13–17% nominal INR capital-cost range, while recent incremental returns are much lower. Excluding uncommissioned CWIP improves a lagged view, but committed money still belongs in the denominator. Persistent poor three-year cash realization caps GQS at 5 despite a real demand runway. The evidence does not yet show a self-funding, high-return reinvestment flywheel.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The principal operating leaders are chairman/CFO Satishkumar Parmar, managing director Dineshkumar Chaudhary and whole-time director Ashokkumar Panchal. March 2026 promoter/group holding was 73.76%, with no disclosed pledge, warrants or ESOPs; 27.75% of promoter shares were locked in, which is not a pledge. Snehal Mehta's July 2026 purchase of 25,000 shares is a favorable alignment data point, but does not establish the entire October promoter register.
FY26 three executive directors received ₹3.60 crore combined, 30.2% of group PAT. Disclosed remuneration to those directors, subsidiary directors and named relatives totals ₹6.1159 crore, about 51.2% of PAT. These are recorded expenses, not an addback or proof of diversion. The USA subsidiary made a ₹0.1905 crore director loan; recovery and terms deserve scrutiny and no recovery value is assumed. September AGM approved broad related-party dealings with wholly owned subsidiaries; the notice's limits are permissions, not actual transactions or third-party revenue. Intercompany elimination limits direct minority leakage, but transfer-pricing and foreign-subsidiary oversight remain relevant.
The prospectus disclosed old stock-record/GST-expense reporting deficiencies. Management proposed ERP implementation and better records; the auditor's February 2024 certificate said the qualifications did not affect the financial numbers. FY26 CARO records physical inventory verification without material discrepancies and an operating audit trail without identified tampering. These are meaningful favorable developments, not proof every old documentation issue is cured. Professional tax over six months remains ₹3.6169 lakh; it is included within statutory obligations, not added twice.
The prospectus described ₹53.48 lakh direct-tax and ₹27.73 lakh indirect-tax matters, disputed by the company, including appellate proceedings. FY26 audit says no disputed statutory dues and its contingent-tax rows are blank; absent closure orders, the earlier matters are historical disclosures, not proven current liabilities. The company's claim against PNB is a potential recovery, not a debt owed by EMMIL, and no recovery is valued. No fraud, conviction or actual default is inferred.
Promises versus delivery: 900-to-1,500 capacity expansion is management-reported complete; January 2026 facility-completion language became June 2026 operation; forecast savings and higher export contribution remain to be demonstrated in audited FY27 cash. FY26 EPS ₹10.54 versus ₹10.47 and lower H2 PAT are weaker than the capacity narrative. Separate disclosure defects include MSME-note versus balance-sheet amounts and a ₹7.17 lakh HDFC loan difference; management attributes the latter to bank non-reflection of prior EMI payments and is seeking correction.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
All amounts below are crore; the attached structured history contains the full six-year inputs, perimeter, audit status, EPS, debt, cash, assets and limitations. FY21/FY22/FY23 restated revenue/PAT were 47.61/0.95, 78.35/3.36 and 99.56/7.90. FY24/FY25/FY26 group revenue/PAT were 126.29/10.97, 151.13/11.86 and 160.85/11.93. Original and restated FY23 profits differ; the prospectus also contains two FY23 CFO figures, 5.5092 detailed versus 5.0324 summary. Both are retained and neither conflict is hidden in a blended cash-conversion average.
Comparable FY24–FY26 reported CFO is -5.0354, -7.6792 and +14.7631, totaling ₹2.0485 crore versus ₹34.7624 crore PAT: only 5.89% cumulative conversion. Cash capex is ₹2.7386, ₹16.5495 and ₹17.5648 crore, totaling ₹36.8529 crore; CFO minus total cash capex is -₹34.8044 crore. Interest is separately financing-classified, so this is not distributable FCFE. Capex explains weak FCF, not weak CFO: receivables, inventory and supplier funding explain the operating cash shortfall.
FY26 PBT ₹16.5711 plus D&A ₹3.9849 plus finance ₹2.6026 less interest income ₹0.0298 gives pre-WC ₹23.1288 crore. Receivable release ₹3.4292 is outweighed by inventory ₹6.2891, fewer payables ₹3.1427, advances and other items; total WC use is ₹3.7295. Reported tax cash is ₹4.6362. The cash statement classifies DTL movement as financing and includes tax provisions in WC. Reclassifying that noncash line, without claiming independently verified tax payments, gives FY26 CFO ₹14.5314 and FY25 -₹7.5743; the poor multi-year conclusion survives.
Operating FY26 EBITDA is ₹22.5167 crore and EBIT ₹18.5318 crore, excluding all ₹0.6419 crore other income. Normalized PAT bridge: reported ₹11.9349 + prior-period tax ₹0.6379 - other income after assumed 25% tax ₹0.481425 = ₹12.091375 crore. Regular remuneration and start-up costs are not removed. FY26 inventory ₹76.2011 crore is 47.4% of annual revenue; receivables ₹13.3975 crore include ₹2.6104 crore older than one year and ₹1.5412 crore older than three, without a bad-debt allowance. Total receivables fell, but the oldest bucket rose. Average receivable days are 34.3; inventory days 266.6 using direct production-cost proxy; payables 51.5 using material purchases. This approximate 249-day cycle is not comparable to management's differently defined working-capital-days claim.
Operating IC is ₹126.7688 crore versus ₹107.1539 crore. It reconciles FY26 equity + debt + income-tax payable + gratuity + accrued interest + deferred tax - available cash - director loan - interest receivable. The ₹19.6149 crore increase also reconciles net capex after D&A ₹13.5799 + ONWC growth ₹6.0174 + bank-margin growth ₹0.0175, within rounding. NOPAT at 25% tax ₹13.89885 gives ROIC 11.88%, ROCE 15.84% and ROE 13.24%. One-year incremental ROIC is 2.65%. Full operating IC from prospectus tax, gratuity, leave and non-operating asset notes is ₹34.2985 crore in FY21 and ₹47.0937 crore in FY23. Five-year incremental NOPAT ₹11.821725 on additional operating IC ₹92.4703 gives 12.78%; three-year ₹5.158125 on ₹79.6751 gives 6.47%. Organic subsidiary establishment is new committed capital, not an external acquisition; the five-year recovery includes a COVID base. A simpler two-year financing-IC cross-check is 1.39%, not a project IRR. This long-window evidence, rather than current ROCE alone, supports CAP 4.
The May 2024 IPO issued 2,982,000 fresh shares at ₹138, raising ₹41.1516 crore gross and ₹37.7902 crore after audited issue costs, with no offer for sale. Bonus-adjusted pre-IPO shares 8,344,500 became 11,326,500, a 35.74% economic share-count increase; the earlier 2:1 bonus itself was not dilution. FY24 PAT on current shares is about ₹9.68 per share, versus FY26 ₹10.54, much less dramatic than growth in assets. Debt ₹29.7114 includes current term maturities ₹3.7220 and cash credit ₹18.1802. Book cash ₹2.9530 includes ₹0.1981 bank-guarantee margin, leaving at most ₹2.7549 before IPO earmarks. Additional obligations are traced individually in claims_ledger.json. The MSME note ₹5.2229 versus balance-sheet ₹4.1351 difference of ₹1.0878 is bounded as a possible reconciliation exposure, not automatically additional debt. CSR required/spent ₹28.28 lakh was visually verified; OCR incorrectly read 98.28 and that error is not treated as a corporate discrepancy.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Market cap is ₹131.22 crore. Standard EV is ₹158.17 crore using drawn debt and cash excluding guarantee margin, before uncertain IPO restriction and legacy non-debt claims. This is 10.99x reported PAT, 10.85x normalized PAT and 7.02x operating EBITDA. If the full last-disclosed IPO earmark remained, standard EV would be ₹1.5651 crore higher. Neither book value nor a peer premium is a liquidation floor.
The five-year model begins with audited March balances and an explicitly unobserved 202-day bridge: flat FY26 operating run rate, unchanged ONWC, ₹3.50 crore additional capex, opening tax/interest settlement and proportionate current maturities. Maximum possible remaining September 2025 IPO earmark ₹1.5651 is reserved from already received cash and spent only on authorized capex, never added as new funding. Bridge cash is ₹3.72 crore under these assumptions. An extra ₹2 crore capex leaves ₹1.72 crore and a modeled 13.75% return; an extra ₹4 crore creates a ₹0.28 crore shortfall and no ordinary IRR. The evidence does not bound actual spending or ONWC within that narrow funded range. June commissioning does not verify the cash bridge, so R and IAS remain NS.
Illustrative base, not a verified current funded case: 8% sales growth each year, EBITDA margin 14–14.5%, 25% normalized cash tax, 2.5% sales D&A, 3.5% sales capex, unchanged 45.35% broad operating-WC intensity, 9.5% cost on drawn debt, no new financing, no dividends, 7x exit EBITDA. Year-five sales/EBITDA ₹236.34/₹34.27 crore; remaining demand debt ₹18.18 crore; retained cash ₹32.83 crore, of which ₹1 crore is withheld as operating cash. After remaining legacy gratuity/DTL claims, equity ₹251.92 crore, ₹222.42 per current diluted share and 13.93% annual return. Term debt is amortized at the disclosed near-term pace as an assumption, not a known full lender schedule.
Bull: 12% growth, EBITDA margin 15–17%, WC intensity 44% down to 40%, capex 4.5% sales and 9x exit. Internally funded in this model; ₹283.47 crore terminal sales and ₹399.93 share value imply 28.12% return. This requires genuine process, mix and cash-conversion gains plus rerating, so is not the base. Linked bear: initial 10% sales fall, margins 10.5–12%, WC intensity 55% easing to 52%, 11.5% debt cost, lower capex and bounded reconciliation claims. It needs ₹1.53 crore funding; ordinary IRR and equity value are withheld. A separately labeled equity rescue at 25% below entry preserves 98.46% ownership and produces ₹87.69 terminal price/-5.42% IRR; actual terms or funding access could be worse.
Base operations at 5x rather than 7x exit yield only 6.92% return. Growth/exit sensitivities at 4% growth are 4.48%/10.90%/16.11% for 5x/7x/9x; at 8%, 6.92%/13.93%/19.55%; at 12%, 9.46%/17.05%/23.08%. These use the same reinvestment and funding rules. At 7x and base margins, the current price needs 9.38% annual growth to earn 15%, or 5.46%/13.19% to earn 12%/18%. Base hurdle-consistent entry prices are ₹126.21/₹110.58/₹97.22 at 12%/15%/18%; they are conditional analytical ranges, not observable fair values or executable orders. With no dividends, all modeled wealth is realized at terminal sale. Two percent aggregate execution friction lowers returns by roughly 0.45 percentage points and is not hidden within a score haircut.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear argument is not that the factory is fictitious or every old tax issue is unresolved. It is that machine variety, slow-moving inventory, limited pricing power and customer-capex cycles can absorb cash faster than accounting profits compound. A new plant can then improve capacity while leaving owners dependent on the bank and fresh equity.
In the linked bear, lower volume and margins coincide with longer collection/production cycles and higher financing cost. A ₹1.53 crore shortfall is modeled, not an observed default; no ordinary equity IRR is shown. Standalone stresses under otherwise base operations give a ₹1.18 crore gap for 15 extra receivable days, ₹2.79 crore for 30 extra inventory days, and ₹2.19 crore for funding replacement after 10% inventory impairment. Half/full cash-credit recall produces ₹3.66/₹12.75 crore gaps, with the recalled debt reduced once, not also left as a terminal claim. These are separate sensitivities, not an unsupported stack assumed inevitable.
The reasonable countercase is important: flat sales, 12.5% EBITDA margin, unchanged WC and ₹3 crore annual essential capex remain funded under the same bridge and debt assumptions. There is no basis to force a funding-failure verdict by requiring all demand debt to be repaid immediately or by adding an arbitrary large buffer. At a 5x exit this restrained case earns approximately 0.07% a year, demonstrating survival is not an attractive return.
Permanent-loss risk is High because an inventory/collections shock can lead to unfavorable recapitalization, liquidation of specialized stock below book value, lost customers and compressed valuation. Cash generated from existing operations and genuinely released inventory could prevent that path. The crucial break variable is sustainable cash conversion after commissioning, not the next capacity announcement. Current funding uncertainty remains an evidence hold.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold wealth in five years require 37.97% and 58.49% annual share-price appreciation before taxes and costs. With a 14.5% EBITDA margin and 7x exit, ignoring net claims for a first-pass hurdle, they require roughly ₹646/₹1,293 crore terminal sales. At an illustrative ₹21 lakh per machine that is around 3,100/6,200 equivalent units, well above management's 1,500-unit annual capacity. Actual debt, working capital, replacement capex and any equity dilution make the test harder, not easier.
Even the funded bull produces about 3.45x ending wealth and relies on better margins, lower WC intensity and 9x valuation. A fivefold outcome could occur with further plants, stronger mix/exports or higher valuation, but no funded evidence-backed path is established. Tenfold is substantially more speculative. Large addressable-market claims or a low quoted share price do not substitute for unit economics and retained ownership.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain FY27 H1 balance sheet and cash flow: verify the March-to-October cash bridge, actual incremental capex and remaining restricted IPO proceeds before considering implementation.
2. Track rolling three-year CFO/PAT from 5.89% toward at least 70%, alongside CFO after interest and maintenance needs. One temporary receivable release is insufficient.
3. Inventory: baseline ₹76.20 crore and about 267 proxy days. Investigate any growth faster than sales, aged stock or borrowing-base exclusions; do not count a write-down as cash collection.
4. Receivables: ₹2.61 crore over one year and ₹1.54 crore over three. Require named aging/recovery evidence or provisioning; watch continued growth in oldest balances despite lower total debtors.
5. Commissioned output: obtain actual monthly machines, utilization, ASP/mix, warranty/rework and dispatch-to-cash data for the claimed 1,500-unit capacity and June 2026 facility.
6. Backward integration: reconcile group job-work baseline ₹6.62 crore and independently track cash savings, labor, depreciation and extra WC rather than the standalone presentation figure alone.
7. Debt: confirm ₹3.722 crore near-term maturities, HDFC bank/books reconciliation, sanctioned/unused headroom and covenant compliance; a bank recall is a thesis-changing event, not a base assumption.
8. Governance: close professional-tax arrears, reconcile the ₹1.0878 crore MSME-note difference, disclose director-loan recovery/terms and monitor actual intercompany dealings against approved ceilings.
9. Orders: verify conversion/cancellation/advances on the ₹47.23 crore book, not just new bookings; monitor repeat business without substituting an unaudited percentage for retained earnings.
10. Execution/liquidity: refresh 60-session actual turnover, current lot, price bands and surveillance indicators before any action; model the user's actual position, spread and costs. Reopen the thesis only when current funding and mature cash returns improve together.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Exact BQS 5.02 is scoreable, but R and IAS are NS. The correct classification is Hold — unresolved current funding evidence; no complete numeric matrix cell can be assigned. GQS 5.00 does not support a compounder designation. This is a research-watchlist cyclical manufacturer with quality limitations, not an investment-ready recommendation, not a blanket assertion of fraud or financial distress, and not an instruction to trade.
Quality comparison eligibility is retained because nine historical/operating factors are supported at Medium confidence or better and bounded accounting issues do not erase their information. Investment ranking eligibility is withheld until the current cash/IPO/lender bridge is verified. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is hypothetical; with a ₹28,962.50 lot, 17 lots cost ₹4,92,362.50 and 18 cost ₹5,21,325.00. At 5% participation and lower 60-day turnover, continuous capacity implies 11.05 sessions; whole-lot median is one lot per session, suggesting 17–18 sessions for those feasible positions before execution risk. At 2% the median daily whole-lot capacity is zero, even though occasional sessions permit trades. Sixty-session mean/median turnover are ₹13.65/₹9.05 lakh, versus recent twenty-session ₹23.53/₹19.11 lakh, with no zero-trade days in either window. Continuous 2%/5%/10% reference capacities imply 27.63/11.05/5.53 sessions. Across sixty sessions, whole-lot capacities total 28/106/243 lots, on only 18/42/54 eligible sessions; at mean whole-lot rates, 17 lots need 36.43/9.62/4.20 sessions and 18 lots 38.57/10.19/4.44. These are different statistics, not interchangeable guaranteed exits. The dated security price range is ₹92.70–₹139.00. REG1 shows active SM, no GSM/ASM/ESM/default flag, but flags fewer than 100 unique PANs and not-regularly-traded SME. Those reference flags do not mean the observed sixty sessions had zero trades. The 19 October EOD indicator file is a next-session reference, not an execution guarantee. Thin liquidity can make a theoretically attractive entry impractical.
The analysis would improve with a verified cash-positive current bridge, explicit IPO completion, recovered old receivables and actual incremental returns above a reasonable capital-cost range. A price near the conditional ₹110.58 base 15% hurdle level alone does not cure weak cash realization or unknown current funding. No suitable position size, buy or exit quantity can be inferred without portfolio context.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source ledger lists dated primary documents, exact URLs, local-file hashes where successfully retrieved and page/section locators. Core financial sources are the FY26 audited annual report, the IPO restated accounts and FY25 audited comparatives. Management presentations are separately labeled; claim dates are not presented as audited realized results. Dated NSE files provide actual traded values, issued shares, active series and lot size, rather than an aggregator's stale volume or guessed lot.
The reproducible model includes yearly revenue, EBITDA, taxes, interest, operating WC, capex, debt, cash, diluted shares and terminal claims; every opening liability is assigned once in the claims ledger. All amounts are nominal INR crore unless stated; normalized operating tax is an assumption of 25%. The 13–17% capital-cost range is an analytical comparison for a small, cyclical, concentrated manufacturer, not an asserted measured WACC; the user-specified equity hurdle remains 15%.
Open questions: October unrestricted and subsidiary cash availability; final IPO-use certificate; a full lender maturity/unused-limit schedule; FY27 H1 cash generation; actual FY26/FY27 output and new-facility economics; inventory aging; old-receivable recoverability; MSME reconciliation; director-loan terms; legal closure orders for old disputes; the full FY24 comparative regrouping bridge; and executable depth/spreads. A six-month-old balance sheet cannot answer those by inference.
Source-acquisition limitations are explicit: the very large FY24/FY25 annual-report downloads were truncated in this execution workspace and are excluded from the verified local-source archive. Their remembered contents are not represented as recovered files. The issuer's smaller FY25 audited PDF was independently read via web and its comparatives reconciled; direct download returned 406. FY21–FY23 restated statements and FY25–FY26 annual data are locally preserved. This limits some older note-level precision, reflected in Medium confidence and proxy bounds, rather than fabricated data or automatic low/default scores.

The 202-day bridge is an assumption, not observed interim cash. Missing FY27 cash evidence is material: canonical R and IAS are NS. All returns here are assumption-dependent illustrations, not a verified current funded opportunity or proof of default.
No new debt, options, warrants, acquired earnings or NCI assumed; two existing subsidiaries are wholly owned.

Term amortization after the disclosed next twelve months repeats 3.722 crore a year until paid: an explicit assumption, not a supplied lender schedule. Drawn cash credit continues at existing amount and is deducted at exit; recall stress reduces both cash and the same debt.

Opening statutory, employee, customer-advance, trade, CSR, bonus and audit balances are in ONWC and roll into replacements once. Opening income tax and accrued interest are paid in bridge only. Gratuity is paid pro rata for its current portion in bridge; remaining legacy claim deducted once at exit. Ongoing gratuity expense is assumed paid as accrued and included in margins. DTL is deducted only at exit.

Potential IPO restriction is reserved out of already received opening cash, then applied only to authorized incremental capex. It is not added again as new financing. Opening CWIP is not repurchased. Bank guarantee margin is unavailable and excluded from added terminal cash.

Director loan recovery is zero in valuation, not an additional liability. MSME disclosure difference 1.0878 and bank difference .071678 crore are stress claims only, not proven extra base debt. CSR note visually verified as 28.28 lakh required and spent; extracted text misread it as 98.28. There is no inferred extra CSR claim.

Operating cash reserve 1 crore is withheld from terminal surplus; annual funding test uses zero, so arbitrary reserve cannot manufacture default. Lower of negative cash and zero is a hypothetical financing shortfall, never an actual default claim.

liquidity.method: Actual NSE turnover, all 60 complete dated market files, absent symbol retained as zero, not missing-file imputation. Whole-lot calculation floors participation times actual daily volume divided by 250; these are theoretical capacities, not promised execution.
